name: 5P49V6965A000NLGI8
title: 5P49V6965 VersaClock 6E programmable clock generator: one PLL, four universal output pairs plus an LVCMOS reference output, I2C and OTP, 24-VFQFPN 4 × 4 mm
summary: A programmable clock generator that makes up to five clocks from one reference: a crystal of 8MHz to 40MHz, or a clock on the crystal input or on a differential input, with glitch-free manual switching between the two. One PLL with a 2.5GHz to 2.9GHz VCO feeds four fractional dividers, each driving an output pair that can be LVPECL, LVDS, HCSL or two LVCMOS outputs, from 1kHz up to 350MHz differential or 200MHz LVCMOS; a fifth pin gives an LVCMOS copy of the reference. Settings live in four banks of OTP, picked by two select pins, or are written over I2C at 0xD0 or 0xD4. The core and each output bank run from 1.8V, 2.5V or 3.3V; RMS phase jitter is 0.5ps typical over 12kHz to 20MHz, and the part is rated for -40°C to +85°C.
key_figures: 4 universal pairs (LVPECL, LVDS, HCSL, 2 × LVCMOS) + 1 LVCMOS reference
crystal 8MHz to 40MHz; CLKIN 1MHz to 350MHz; single-ended on XIN 1MHz to 200MHz
4 OTP banks; I2C at 0xD0 or 0xD4, up to 400kHz

circuits.title: Crystal oscillator and load capacitors
circuits.description: A fundamental-mode crystal Y1 sits between XIN/REF and XOUT. Inside the chip an inverting amplifier with a feedback resistor RF and a series resistor RS drives it, and the programmable capacitors Ci1 (at XIN) and Ci2 (at XOUT) set most of the load. Each pin also carries 1pF to 3pF of stray capacitance (Cs1, Cs2). Ce1 and Ce2 are optional external capacitors to ground that add load; they lower the oscillator gain, so the factory is to be consulted before fitting them.

circuits.title: Overdriving XIN with a CMOS driver
circuits.description: An LVCMOS clock source drives XIN/REF in place of a crystal. Its output resistance Ro plus a series resistor Rs make 50 Ω to match the line. At the far end R1 and R2 divide the swing down to about 1V peak, and the 1nF capacitor C3 couples it into XIN/REF. XOUT is left open. R1 and R2 depend on the driver supply: 130 Ω and 75 Ω at 3.3V, 100 Ω and 100 Ω at 2.5V, 62 Ω and 130 Ω at 1.8V.

circuits.title: Overdriving XIN with an LVPECL driver
circuits.description: A +3.3V LVPECL driver feeds XIN/REF from one side of its output. Both outputs run down 50 Ω lines and are terminated in the usual LVPECL way: R1 and R2, 50 Ω each, to a common node that R3 (50 Ω) takes to ground. The true side is AC-coupled into XIN/REF through the 1nF capacitor C1; XOUT is left open. For a 2.5V LVPECL driver only R3 changes.

circuits.title: Driving CLKIN with an LVCMOS driver
circuits.description: An LVCMOS source drives the differential CLKIN input single-ended. Ro plus Rs make 50 Ω to match the line, so the full LVCMOS swing crosses the line; at CLKIN the divider R1 and R2 cuts it to under the 1.2V peak-to-peak limit. CLKINB goes to ground. R1 and R2 depend on the driver supply: 130 Ω and 75 Ω at 3.3V, 100 Ω and 100 Ω at 2.5V, 62 Ω and 130 Ω at 1.8V.

circuits.title: CLKIN, CLKINB driven by an HCSL driver
circuits.description: An HCSL source drives CLKIN and CLKINB directly over two 50 Ω lines, DC-coupled; the input also takes LVPECL and LVDS this way.

circuits.title: LVDS standard termination
circuits.description: One output pair, set to LVDS, drives a differential line whose impedance Zo is close to ZT. A single resistor ZT across the pair at the receiver terminates it; ZT is 90 Ω to 132 Ω, chosen to match Zo, 100 Ω in a typical design. The resistor is a surface-mount part placed right at the receiver. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

parts.note: differential transmission line, pins INP/INN at the driver end, OUTP/OUTN at the far end

circuits.title: LVDS optional termination
circuits.description: The same LVDS link with the terminating resistor split into two halves of ZT/2. A capacitor C of about 50pF from their centre tap to ground filters common-mode noise. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: 3.3V LVPECL output termination (1)
circuits.description: An output pair set to LVPECL at VDDO = 3.3V drives two 50 Ω lines. At the receiver R1 and R2, 50 Ω each, join at a node that RTT (50 Ω) returns to ground, giving the DC path the LVPECL outputs need. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: 3.3V LVPECL output termination (2)
circuits.description: An output pair set to LVPECL at VDDO = 3.3V drives two 50 Ω lines, each ended at the receiver by a divider from 3.3V to ground: 125 Ω up (R3, R4) and 84 Ω down (R1, R2). The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: 2.5V LVPECL output termination
circuits.description: An output pair set to LVPECL at VDDO = 2.5V drives two 50 Ω lines, each ended at the receiver by a divider from 2.5V to ground: 250 Ω up (R1, R3) and 62.5 Ω down (R2, R4). The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: 2.5V LVPECL driver termination (1)
circuits.description: At VDDO = 2.5V the LVPECL termination voltage VDDO - 2V is close to ground, so each 50 Ω line ends in a 50 Ω resistor (R1, R2) straight to ground. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: 2.5V LVPECL driver termination (2)
circuits.description: At VDDO = 2.5V the two 50 Ω lines end in R1 and R2, 50 Ω each, joined at a node that R3 (18 Ω) returns to ground. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: HCSL receiver terminated
circuits.description: An output pair set to HCSL, at VDDO of 3.3V or 2.5V, drives two 50 Ω lines through 33 Ω series resistors. Each line ends at the receiver in 50 Ω to ground. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: HCSL source terminated
circuits.description: An output pair set to HCSL drives two 50 Ω lines; the 50 Ω resistors to ground sit at the source, just after the 33 Ω series resistors, and the lines run unterminated to the receiver. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

circuits.title: LVCMOS termination
circuits.description: An output pair in CMOSD mode (two CMOS outputs, 180 degrees apart) drives two 50 Ω lines through 33 Ω series resistors into a receiver. The driver can be any of the output pairs OUT1 to OUT4.

operation.text: One PLL with a VCO of 2500MHz to 2900MHz is locked to a single reference, taken from either the crystal oscillator (XIN/REF, XOUT) or the differential input (CLKIN, CLKINB). Four fractional output dividers (FOD1 to FOD4) each feed one output pair, OUT1 to OUT4; OUT0 is an LVCMOS copy of the reference. OTP memory and control logic hold up to four configurations, reached through the select pins or I2C.

An internal power-on reset circuit starts the part once every VDD pin is supplied. The level on OUT0_SEL_I2CB at reset picks one of two modes. Low gives software mode: the I2C port is open and the default configuration can be rewritten in the system at any time. High gives hardware select mode: the OTP is loaded at power-up (REG0[7] = 1) as the power-up behavior table lists. The default configuration of either mode can be programmed by the user or at the factory.

In hardware select mode the OTP holds up to four configurations, chosen by SEL1 and SEL0. Their levels must be settled at reset so the chosen configuration loads. After the first 10ms they may be changed between ground and VDDD/VDDA, one pin at a time, with edges faster than 300ns; after each change the part needs 1ms undisturbed for the new values to load and take effect.

There are two reference inputs. The crystal input also accepts a single-ended clock. CLKIN/CLKINB is a fully differential clock-only input that takes LVDS, HCSL and LVPECL levels with no external termination, and a CMOS clock of up to 1.2V on CLKIN. Using CLKIN needs the en_clkin register bit set. Both inputs may float when unused. The crystal oscillator is on by default and can be turned off when not used.

With SM[1:0] = 0x the redundant inputs are in manual switchover: the CLKSEL pin moves between the primary and secondary reference, and the PRIMSRC bit (register 0x13 bit 1) sets which is which, so it also reverses the CLKSEL polarity. The output does not glitch during a switch, but frequency and phase may drift depending on how the two references relate.

A crystal is cut to its nominal frequency at a stated load capacitance. An oscillator load below that value raises the frequency and a load above it lowers it, so the load is matched to the crystal. The internal capacitors Ci1 and Ci2 are a fixed part plus a part set by XTAL[5:0], from 0pF to 13.83pF in 0.43pF steps, and are normally given the same value; this lets crystals from many makers be used. Adding Ce1 or Ce2 increases the load but reduces oscillator gain, which can stop the crystal starting; the factory is to be consulted before adding them.
The PLL loop bandwidth is programmable and its range depends on the reference frequency: 40kHz to 126kHz at a 1MHz reference, 300kHz to 1000kHz at 350MHz.

Each FOD counts with a 12-bit integer part and a 24-bit fractional part. Integer-only division gives the best performance; the fractional counters set an output frequency to within 50ppb. A divider can also bypass (divide by 1), giving a buffered copy of the input or of another FOD, and FODs can be cascaded to reach lower output frequencies.

Each divider can spread its own output to lower EMI, with triangle modulation at 30kHz to 63kHz, independent of output frequency. Spread is available on outputs of 5MHz to 300MHz, programmable from ±0.1% to ±2.5% centre spread or from -0.2% to -5% down spread. Misprint: the smallest settings are also given as ±0.25% and -0.5%; they should read ±0.1% and -0.2%.

Every output divider has a synchronising pulse so the outputs start aligned. In hardware select mode the outputs align at power-on reset and again on each change of configuration through SEL0/SEL1. Rewriting a divider over I2C in software mode can lose alignment, which an I2C-triggered reset restores. Falling edges are aligned by default; rising-edge alignment comes from skewing the faster clock by 180 degrees.

Each output can be skewed from 0 to 360 degrees in steps of 1/32 of the VCO period, so the step in degrees varies with VCO and output frequency; for a 100MHz output with a 2800MHz VCO the step is 11.161ps, or 0.402 degrees.

Each output pair is set on its own to LVPECL or HCSL at 2.5V or 3.3V, or LVDS or LVCMOS at 1.8V, 2.5V or 3.3V, and VDDO supplies may be mixed. LVCMOS has four modes: CMOSD (OUTx and OUTxB in antiphase), CMOSX2 (both in phase), CMOS1 (OUTx only) and CMOS2 (OUTxB only); in the two-pin modes both pins share the same settings. Each output has its own enable bit, and a disabled output sits at logic 1 or Hi-Z. An output is off when turned off over I2C, when turned off by SD/OE, or when it is marked unused, which keeps it off whatever OE does.

SD/OE is programmed as an output enable or a global shutdown, either active low or active high. What a disabled output does is programmable too: OUTx high with OUTxB low, or both Hi-Z, under the control of the SD/OE pin or set over I2C.

The part is an I2C slave at address 0xD0 or 0xD4, so two can share a bus. Transfers are byte-oriented block writes and reads: two address bytes give the first register, and data bytes follow in ascending register order, most significant bit first. A transfer may stop after any whole byte. Written data reaches the registers only at the STOP condition, all bytes at once. External pull-up resistors on SDA and SCL are needed for full I2C electrical compliance. A current read is S, device address + R, then data bytes each acknowledged, a not-acknowledge and P; a sequential read writes the register start address after device address + W, then a repeated start and device address + R; a sequential write sends device address + W, the register start address and the data bytes, then P.

Used as a crystal input, XIN/REF and XOUT connect to a crystal. An unused LVCMOS output may float with no trace attached, its buffer set to high impedance to avoid noise. Unused differential outputs may float the same way, no trace and buffers in Hi-Z; the two halves of a pair are treated alike, both floating or both terminated.

XIN/REF accepts a clock of 500mV to 1.2V amplitude with a slew rate above 0.2V/ns, for better SNR or to use input selection with CLKIN. An LVCMOS source may drive it, or a single leg of a differential source through a series AC-coupling capacitor; XOUT may float. With a clock on XIN the load capacitors are set to 0.

All parts of the LVPECL-to-XIN interface are placed in the layout even if some go unused, as they help in debugging. The specifications are characterised and guaranteed with a quartz crystal as the input. A 2.5V LVPECL driver needs only a different R3.

CLKIN has a 1.2V regulated input inside, so it cannot take more than 1.2V peak-to-peak; it is AC coupled inside, so LVDS and LVPECL are accepted. For an LVCMOS source, Ro + Rs match the 50 Ω line, the line carries the full LVCMOS level for best S/N, and the R1-R2 divider keeps Vrx peak-to-peak under 1.2V. A slower or weaker driver can be loaded less by raising the divider impedance.

The termination ZT is 90 Ω to 132 Ω and matches the differential line impedance Zo; a typical point-to-point link uses 100 Ω across the receiver on a 100 Ω line. Surface-mount parts placed close to the receiver avoid reflections. The receiver's amplitude and common-mode input range are to be verified against the LVDS output, and a non-standard termination is to be confirmed with the factory.

LVPECL outputs need a DC path to ground through the terminating resistors, or current sources, to work. They drive 50 Ω lines and need matched-impedance routing for best speed and signal shape. At VDDO = 2.5V the VDDO - 2V level is near ground, so R3 of the 2.5V termination can be left out.
The HCSL terminations apply at VDDO of both 3.3V and 2.5V.
